subject.title: Feature: support message read action for Telegram

question: Should OpenClaw expose recent Telegram chat content through `message read`, and what retention, authorization, and default action gate should that read path use?
rationale: The missing surface is clear, but the durable product choice is not mechanical because Telegram bots only receive observed updates and the implementation would expose retained chat content to agent tooling.

options.title: Bounded gated read action
options.body: Add Telegram-owned `read` support using a bounded observed-message store with an explicit action/config gate, conservative retention, docs, tests, and live proof.

options.title: Wait for passive archive API
options.body: Defer explicit Telegram reads until the public skipped-message observation contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83101 or a successor is approved and landed.

options.title: Do not expose Telegram reads
options.body: Keep Telegram limited to send/edit/delete/react/topic actions and direct users to plugin-owned archive integrations for history retrieval.

recommendation.title: Bounded gated read action
recommendation.body: Add Telegram-owned `read` support using a bounded observed-message store with an explicit action/config gate, conservative retention, docs, tests, and live proof.
